body:
When importing the default `icon.svg` as Texture2DArray with lossless or lossy compression, 3 horizontal slices, and any number of vertical slices, clicking reimport would result in the error:
`ERROR: servers/rendering/renderer_rd/storage_rd/texture_storage.cpp:879 - Condition "p_layers[i]->get_format() != valid_format" is true.` ([Source code mentioned in error](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/eb72ce2db4b67acbc77548e5a5a7f61af657660b/servers/rendering/renderer_rd/storage_rd/texture_storage.cpp#L879))
What this error means is that the format of one layer is different from the format of another layer. When importing as previously mentioned, layer 0 and layer 2 would be saved with RGBA8 format, and layer 1 would be saved with RGB8 format, resulting in different formats, producing the error.

The reason that the layers were in different formats was because it was saved in WebP image. The error could be bypassed by saving it as a PNG (i.e. changing the `force png` setting to true). The reason why saving as a WebP image caused the error was because WebP checks if that image contains alpha pixels, and saves the image with RGBA8 (*contains alpha channel*) if it contains alpha pixels, and as RGB8 (*without an alpha channel*) if the image doesn't contain alpha pixels. ([Source code for WebP saving](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/eb72ce2db4b67acbc77548e5a5a7f61af657660b/modules/webp/webp_common.cpp#L63))

The reason why this error doesn't happen when saving as a PNG is because PNG saves the file with the original format of the image using `source_image->get_format()`. ([Source code for PNG saving](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/eb72ce2db4b67acbc77548e5a5a7f61af657660b/drivers/png/png_driver_common.cpp#L141))

The changes in this pull request are designed to fix the previously mentioned error by changing the the way the WebP chooses the format to saves in. After modifying the code, the way that the WebP chooses its format is now similar to the way the PNG chooses its format. The changes also have to change how the WebP loads (unpacks) the image. The _webp_unpack function now takes the format that it was saved with instead of looking at if it contains an alpha channel.
